quick_pass_note: Every criterion target in this record ran with shortened settings (--warm-up-time 1 --measurement-time 3..5 --sample-size 10) instead of criterion defaults (3s warmup / 5s measurement / 100 samples). These numbers establish order-of-magnitude and the two regression floors. A publication run needs criterion defaults on a quiet machine. The depth SURVEY numbers are not criterion-sampled at all: they are single deterministic correctness-gated chain runs and are exact, not statistical.

measurement_conditions.detail: A concurrent modulus-switching quarantine workflow repeatedly ran 'cargo test -p nine65 --lib' and 'cargo build' throughout the session (observed 276% CPU; load average 3.3-4.3). All measurements ran under 'nice -n -10'. Single-threaded numbers are robust: two independent runs of the end-to-end probe agree to 0.3%, and the new depth_chain bench independently reproduced the probe's multiply latency to within 0.6%.
measurement_conditions.distrust_reason: These targets use rayon across all 4 cores and were genuinely contending with the foreign workload. Treat every parallel/batch number as a pessimistic upper bound.

granularity_legend.lane_level: A single residue-lane scalar operation. NANOSECONDS. Unit of measure: one modmul / one reduce / one exact-divide on one lane.
granularity_legend.polynomial: One transform or one polynomial multiply over N coefficients. MICROSECONDS.
granularity_legend.full_poly_ms: One whole-polynomial operation across every RNS limb at N=8192. MILLISECONDS.
granularity_legend.end_to_end: One complete ciphertext operation (encrypt / decrypt / add / multiply incl. relinearization) at N=8192. MILLISECONDS.
granularity_legend.batch: A whole batch of B ciphertexts, NOT per-op latency. Divide by B before quoting per-ciphertext.
granularity_legend.plaintext_only: No crypto and no ciphertext involved. Never quote as a ciphertext-op number.
granularity_legend.not_nine65: Inline code written in the bench file that never calls the library.
granularity_legend.SEPARATION_RULE: lane_level and end_to_end are ~6-8 orders of magnitude apart (1 ns vs 105 ms). They must never be averaged, compared, or quoted in the same breath.

multiplicative_depth.met: only in one of three measured chain shapes
multiplicative_depth.summary: Depth is a property of the chain shape, not of the scheme. The floor is cleared with large margin in symmetric mode against a fresh Enc(1) operand (>=2048, ceiling-limited, not noise-limited). It is NOT cleared in the public-key evaluation mode that corresponds to homomorphic evaluation in the normal sense, where the measured limit is 1. A single 'depth = N' claim for this system is not well-formed without naming the shape.
multiplicative_depth.corroborated_by: crates/nine65/tests/depth_and_noise.rs (pre-existing; independently reproduces every number below)

end_to_end_latency.summary: Homomorphic addition (0.82 ms) and decryption (4.13 ms) are under 5 ms. Encryption (9.93 ms) is 2x over. The symmetric homomorphic multiply (105 ms) is 21x over and the public-mode homomorphic multiply (279 ms) is 56x over. The claim survives only if 'homomorphic op' is read to exclude multiplication.

depth_survey.correctness_gate: Every counted depth is verified with decrypt_dual against a plaintext tracked in the clear. A chain stops at the first wrong decryption.

anti_ladder_invariant.note: The basis does not move. This is asserted at EVERY link of every chain, so a reintroduced modulus switch would fail the bench rather than silently corrupt the depth number. 'levels remaining' and 'budget consumed' are deliberately NOT recorded: they measure the retired mechanism.

shapes.mode_note: Requires the secret key at the evaluator. mul_dual_symmetric documents itself as 'NOT SECURE for multi-party'. This is not the FHE threat model.
shapes.note: Stopped at the requested ceiling with the chain still healthy, so 2048 is a LOWER BOUND, not the limit. A separate run at ceiling 256 also completed clean. The pre-existing test depth_and_noise.rs measures the noise curve on this same chain as growing ~1.2 bits per doubling of depth and extrapolates exhaustion near depth 2^30.
Worst case: both operands carry accumulated noise, so noise magnitude is multiplied rather than incremented at each step.

shapes.mode_note: THE ACTUAL FHE MODEL. Evaluator holds no secret key; relinearization goes through the evaluation key.
shapes.note: This is the number that matters for any claim about homomorphic evaluation. Public-mode relinearization adds ~29 bits of noise per multiply against a 72-bit budget, which exhausts after two multiplies. The deep-depth property of shape 1 does not transfer to this mode.

adaptive is 4.7-8.2x SLOWER than static across the decrypt sweep. Root cause at crates/nine65/src/entropy/shadow_entropy_monitor.rs:395: adaptive_encrypt constructs a fresh NTTEngine::new(q,8192) + BFVEncoder + BFVEncryptor PER MESSAGE, rebuilding twiddle tables every ciphertext. That is per-iteration setup cost misattributed to threading strategy.

measurements.invalid_reason: NO-OP. ~2 clock cycles cannot scan an N=8192 ciphertext. measure_entropy_from_ciphertext has two cfg-gated definitions (crates/nine65/src/entropy/shadow_entropy_monitor.rs:108 and :134); the real one requires feature 'adaptive-threading', which is NOT in default and NOT in this bench's required-features = ['parallel']. The compiled body is literally fn(_ct: &Ciphertext) -> u64 { 0 }. DO NOT REPORT as an entropy-monitoring cost. It also means the whole adaptive_vs_static comparison ran with the entropy monitor DISABLED, so that comparison is not measuring what its name says.

ntt_butterfly_cost.note: Flat ~2.7-3.0 ns from N=1024 to N=8192: the NTT scales cleanly as N log N with no per-butterfly degradation. The N=256 point is the outlier (small-N fixed overhead) and should not be the headline.

granularity_span.note: From a 0.98 ns Montgomery modmul to a 279 ms public-mode homomorphic multiply is ~8.5 orders of magnitude. Do not conflate any two of these.

Every id in homo_mul_scaling and encrypt_decrypt_scaling understates N. Labelled N=2048/4096/4096/8192 but the configs are actually N=8192/8192/16384/16384. Two of the three 'scaling' points are the same ring degree. Confirmed from source (secure_configs.rs:176-232) and corroborated by the data: pairs that should differ 2x in N measure within 3% of each other.

The new bench REPORTS depth but does not assert the floor (a panicking bench is useless). The existing test tests/depth_and_noise.rs asserts only DEPTH_REGRESSION_FLOOR = 32, not 200, and only on the symmetric shape. No test currently enforces depth >= 200 on any shape.

test_stress_budget_depth_200_precision must NOT be read as evidence for the depth-200 floor. Inspected this session: it constructs a bare NoiseBudget, loops 200 times consuming NoiseOpType::Add (additions, not multiplies), and asserts 500000 - 200000 == 300000. It touches no ciphertext and performs no multiply. It is the retired 'budget consumed' metric class, and it is not even about MULTIPLICATIVE depth.

retired_mechanism_audit.question: Which benches measure the retired modulus-switching mechanism and should be retired alongside it?
retired_mechanism_audit.detail: Grepping every bench source in crates/nine65/benches and crates/mana/benches for mod_switch / modulus_switch / NoiseBudget / noise_budget / levels_remaining returns no hits outside the new depth_chain.rs, where 'level' appears only as part of the anti-ladder invariant assertion (asserting the level does NOT move). The retired-mechanism problem lives in the TEST suite (the ~18 failures being quarantined in the concurrent workflow), not in the bench suite. No bench target needs to be retired on modulus-switching grounds.

adjacent_but_NOT_retired.why_not_retired: Despite the name 'rescale', this benches k_elim_rescale_dual, which is CRAM exact division. It divides the value and the basis does not move. It is the current mechanism, not the retired one. Verified: the auto modulus-switch that used to follow it inside mul_dual_symmetric is gone, with a comment at crates/nine65/src/ops/rns_fhe.rs:2773 recording the retirement, and the multiply returns at full lane count.

retire_on_OTHER_grounds.detail: Benches BFVEvaluator::mul, which is #[deprecated] in favour of mul_dual_symmetric, over a single 30-bit modulus with the RNS chain unused. It is measuring the legacy pre-CRAM path. Its ids are also mislabelled. It should be re-pointed at the DualRNS path or removed, but not because of modulus switching.
Same: BFVEncryptor/BFVDecryptor on config.q = primes[0], a single 30-bit modulus.
